meta.headline: No official source reviewed imposes any tax on the act of converting RMB into USD. The 'conversion penalty' is not one thing — it decomposes into six distinct costs, and the largest ones are triggered by non-reporting and by mis-describing the source of funds, not by converting.
meta.rule: A cost row carries a number ONLY if an official source fixes that number. Everywhere else the value cell is blank and the row is marked UNVERIFIED — no estimate is invented.

components.component: Chinese tax on the currency conversion itself
components.basis: No provision imposing a tax on FX conversion was found in 汇发〔2020〕14号, PBoC Order [2006] No.3, the IIT Law or the FX Regulations. SAFE's own procedure treats conversion as a permitted, documented service, not a taxable event.
components.note: This is the single most important correction to the user's premise: you are not being taxed to convert. You are being gated, taxed on the underlying income, and (potentially) penalised for non-reporting.

components.component: Chinese IIT on the underlying income or gain (paid before you are allowed to remit)
components.value: 20% flat on property transfer, interest, dividends, rent and incidental income; 3%-45% progressive on comprehensive income; 5%-35% on business income
components.basis: IIT Law Art.3 (2018 amendment). The taxable base for a property transfer is proceeds less original cost and reasonable expenses (Art.6(5)).
components.note: This is a real, large cost — but it is tax on the gain, not on the conversion. It is also unavoidable: a tax clearance certificate is a mandatory attachment for 移民转移 (S04 Art.8(6)) and for property-sale remittance (S05 Art.5).

components.component: Tax filing (服务贸易等项目对外支付税务备案) on overseas payments above USD 50,000
components.value: Administrative step, not a tax. Threshold: USD 50,000 per single payment.
components.basis: SAT/SAFE Announcement 2013 No.40 Art.1. Applies to a foreign individual's work remuneration, dividends, interest, royalties, non-capital-transfer gifts, indemnities and incidental income, and to real-property transfer income and equity-transfer gains.
components.note: A gate, not a charge — but it is the step that most often derails a remittance, because it is filed with the tax bureau, not the bank.

components.component: Onshore bank FX bid-ask spread (购汇价差)
components.basis: No official source publishes the spread. It is set commercially by each bank and varies by currency pair, ticket size, channel and customer tier.
components.note: UNVERIFIED — deliberately blank. Obtain a live quote in writing from your bank before modelling anything. Any percentage quoted on a blog is not a source.

components.component: Wire, cable, intermediary-bank and receiving-bank fees
components.basis: Commercially set; no official tariff. Intermediary banks can deduct unpredictably on a correspondent chain.
components.note: UNVERIFIED — blank. Ask for the full fee schedule including correspondent deductions.

components.component: Offshore conversion spread, if you first move RMB out as cash or CNH
components.basis: Commercially set; wide and opaque in retail channels outside Hong Kong.
components.note: UNVERIFIED — blank. Note that this is strictly worse than converting onshore: you pay a spread twice.

components.component: US income tax on the income or gain (worldwide taxation of a US citizen)
components.basis: The filing obligation is not in doubt; the rate depends on your bracket, holding period, exclusions and credits, none of which are knowable here.
components.note: UNVERIFIED rate — blank. The obligation itself is structural. A foreign tax credit for Chinese tax paid is the main relief mechanism; the specific credit rules were not retrieved in this session.

components.component: US tax on the FX movement itself (IRC §988)
components.value: USD 200 de minimis threshold for personal transactions
components.basis: §988(e)(1): the section does not apply to an individual's personal transaction. §988(e)(2): no gain is recognised on a personal transaction in nonfunctional currency unless the gain would exceed USD 200.
components.note: Practically: a personal conversion of your own savings is not meant to generate US income. The consequence cuts both ways — a personal FX LOSS is likewise not deductible. Confirm the characterisation with a CPA; the interaction of (e)(1) and (e)(2) is genuinely technical.

components.component: FBAR non-willful penalty (per violation, per year)
components.value: USD 16,536 maximum, for penalties assessed on or after 2025-01-17
components.basis: 31 CFR 1010.821 Table 1, row 31 U.S.C. 5321(a)(5)(B)(i). Inflation-adjusted annually.
components.note: Per year, per account failure. This dwarfs the FX spread on almost any realistic balance, and it applies whether or not you ever convert a single yuan.

components.component: FBAR willful penalty (per violation, per year)
components.value: USD 165,353 maximum, for penalties assessed on or after 2025-01-17
components.note: The statute also contains an alternative willful measure — the greater of USD 100,000 or 50% of the account balance — but that provision was not retrieved end-to-end in this session, so it is FLAGGED and not given a verified value.

components.value: USD 10,000, plus up to USD 50,000 for a continuing failure
components.basis: 26 U.S.C. §6038D(d)(1) and (d)(2). A reasonable-cause exception exists at §6038D(g).
components.note: Separate from, and additive to, the FBAR penalty for the same account.

components.component: Form 3520 penalty for an unreported large foreign gift or bequest
components.basis: The 5%-per-month / 25%-of-gift penalty rule is widely cited under §6039F, and the IRS Form 3520 instructions were retrieved, but the specific penalty paragraph was not read in this session.
components.note: UNVERIFIED — blank. See the Flagged page.

components.component: SAFE fine for 逃汇 (evading FX controls to move money out)
components.value: Up to 30% of the amount; if serious, 30% up to 100% of the amount; plus an order to repatriate
components.basis: FX Regulations (国务院令第532号) Art.39.
components.note: This is the cost of getting the route wrong. It applies to the AMOUNT, not the gain — which is why 'clever' routes are catastrophically uneconomic.

components.component: SAFE fine for 非法套汇 (illegal arbitrage / obtaining FX on false documents)
components.value: Up to 30% of the amount; if serious, 30% up to 100% of the amount; funds ordered re-exchanged
components.note: The provision SAFE cites for false-document transfers, including under 汇发〔2004〕16号 Art.13.

components.component: SAFE fine for 私自买卖外汇 / 变相买卖外汇 (private or disguised FX trading)
components.value: Warning, confiscation of proceeds, up to 30% of the amount; if serious, 30% up to 100%; criminal liability if it constitutes a crime
components.note: This is the provision that reaches underground banks and crypto-based conversion.

components.component: SAFE fine for carrying FX in or out of the country in breach of the rules
components.value: Warning and up to 20% of the amount
components.note: Relevant to cash-carry strategies and to splitting trips.

components.component: Time and FX-exposure cost of the staged emigrant-transfer payout
components.value: Up to 24 months (50% first, then half the remainder at 12 months, balance at 24 months); RMB 200,000 or less may be remitted in one go
components.note: Not a tax, but a genuine financial cost: you are forced to take the exchange rate at three fixed future dates you do not control. This is usually underweighted in comparisons against the C01 route.

components.component: Added 2026 identity-verification friction on outbound remittances
components.value: Triggers at RMB 5,000 or USD 1,000 equivalent per single outbound remittance
components.basis: PBoC Order [2025] No.11 Art.34, effective 2026-01-01. Remitter identity must be verified accurately; name, account, address and payee details must be carried with the payment; records kept 10 years.
components.note: Not a tax and not a cap — it is a data-quality gate. It does, however, make name/address mismatches between your Chinese account and your US bank a common cause of rejection.

scenarios.note: Total-cost illustrations are NOT provided, because two of the largest inputs (bank spread, wire fees) are commercially set and unverified. Providing a total would be fabrication. The structure below shows which costs apply to which route.

K2 (estate level), K3, K4, K5, K7, K8, K18
K4 (if buying FX first), K6, K16 (if over limit)
